issues.body: The change adds `RemoteDisconnected` to `make_fetch`'s retry arm, but no plan-snapshot self-test makes `urlopen` raise that exception and proves three attempts, the 5/10-second sleeps, and the terminal `FetchError`. The existing shared-taxonomy self-test only proves that `http_transient.is_transient_network(RemoteDisconnected(...))` returns true; it does not prove `make_fetch` consults that classifier or catches this exception. Deleting the newly added tuple member therefore leaves the suite green while restoring the reported whole-tick failure. This also writes the network exception decision locally even though `http_transient.py` explicitly defines `is_transient_network` as the single shared taxonomy and describes a caller-private copy as half-consolidated.
issues.fix_hint: Drive `make_fetch` through a patched `urlopen` that raises a real `RemoteDisconnected`, patch `time.sleep`, and assert the exact attempt count, delays, and final `FetchError`; include a success-on-later-attempt case if appropriate. Wire the call site to the already-loaded `http_transient.is_transient_network` predicate (with identity/delegation pinned) instead of adding another local exception list, while preserving and explicitly testing any intentionally broader legacy `URLError` behavior. Verify that deleting or conditionally bypassing the new guard makes the row fail without aborting the suite.
issues.title: RemoteDisconnected retry path has no non-vacuous call-site test

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The new recovery path is plausible, but it is not independently exercised at the plan-snapshot call site and it reintroduces a private exception taxonomy despite this module already loading the shared transient-network classifier. The added tuple member can be deleted with the existing self-tests remaining green, so the marquee behavior is not protected.
